links.note: Greek says “having”; English recasts the possession as “whose.”
Greek adds “into the middle”; English only says “stand up.”
English specifies origin with “from around”; Greek says “around.”
The middle verb means to call people to oneself.
Greek “those with him” identifies his associates.
Greek “was beside himself” is rendered “is insane.”
Greek uses a future form in this general condition.
Greek specifies plundering his possessions; English leaves the object implicit.
English recasts the recipients of forgiveness as possessors of the sins.
